catalog.summary: Retrieve audit events (large responses — see description)
Search audit events (large responses — see description)

getAuditEvents.description:
Minimum role: Tenant Auditor.

Retrieves audit events for the tenant associated with the authenticated user. Use `type` to filter by event category. Use `dateFrom`/`dateTo` for a specific date range, or `intervalInHours` for a rolling window. The queried range cannot exceed 30 days. If no date filter is supplied, the previous 30 days are returned. Use `limit` and `offset` for pagination (the documented limit cap of 10000 is not enforced server-side — see the `limit` parameter).

**HIGH VOLUME** — audit events are unbounded. A single busy hour can exceed 1,500 events (~825 KB). With no date filter, the default window is the previous 30 days. With no `limit`, a client that auto-follows `meta.paging` merges every page into one response and overflows its token budget. Always pass an explicit `limit` (start small, ~50–100) and narrow the query with `type` plus a tight time range (`intervalInHours`/`interval` or explicit dates). To sweep the full set, hand-page with `limit`+`offset` or filter server-side — never pull a whole window in one call. CEF output (`Accept: text/plain`) ignores `limit`/`offset` and always returns the entire window.

Set `Accept: text/plain` to receive results in Common Event Format (CEF). Default is `application/json`.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Type of events to return. Each value filters to events whose `eventTypeId` carries a matching prefix. Accepted values: `all` (every event), `user_activity` (`USR-*`), `access_control` (`AUTHZ-*`), `int` (integrations, `INT-*`), `conn_mgmt` (connection / SAML management, `CONN-*`), `comment` (`COMMENT-*`), `byok` (Bring Your Own Key encryption), `plan_iq` (PlanIQ), and `forecaster`. A `workflow` category exists for the Workflow product but is omitted from the enum (product not enabled on the test tenant). Omitting the parameter is equivalent to `all` (the default). The enum is not enforced server-side — an unrecognised value is treated as `all` rather than rejected.

parameters.name: dateFrom
parameters.description: Start of the event date range (Unix timestamp in milliseconds, UTC). The span between `dateFrom` and `dateTo` cannot exceed 30 days — a wider range returns 400 `FAILURE_BAD_REQUEST`.

parameters.name: dateTo
parameters.description: End of the event date range (Unix timestamp in milliseconds, UTC). The span between `dateFrom` and `dateTo` cannot exceed 30 days — a wider range returns 400 `FAILURE_BAD_REQUEST`.

parameters.name: intervalInHours
parameters.description: Return events from the previous N hours. For example, `2` returns the last two hours of events. Bound by the same 30-day cap as the date range: a value above `720` (30 days) returns 400 `FAILURE_BAD_REQUEST`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of results to return per page. The documented cap of 10000 is not enforced server-side — larger limits are honored and return more than 10000 records.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Zero-based index of the first result to return. Use with `limit` for pagination.

schema.description: Response envelope for audit event list and search endpoints.

paging.description: Pagination metadata included in audit event list responses.

totalSize.description: Total number of results matching the query.

offSet.description: Zero-based index of the first result in this page.

nextOffset.description: Offset to use to retrieve the next page, if more results exist.

previousUrl.description: URL to call to retrieve the previous page of results. Present once paging past the first page (offset > 0).

userId.description: Identifier of the user who performed the action. Regular user IDs are 32-character lowercase hex strings. Events generated by internal system processes carry an `INTERNAL_` prefix followed by a numeric identifier.

objectId.description: Identifier of the object acted upon. Format varies by object type. Model, workspace, and user objects use a 32-character lowercase hex string. Connection objects (CONN-* events) use a `con_` prefix followed by a base62 string. Absent when no specific object is associated with the event.

objectTypeId.description: Type of the object acted upon, if applicable.

objectTenantId.description: Tenant identifier of the object acted upon — 32-character lowercase hex string. Typically matches `tenantId` for objects within the same tenant.

additionalAttributes.description: Event-type-specific attributes as a free-form map. Keys vary by event type. The API may return an explicit `null` for this field (observed on some `USR-8` login events), so treat it as optional rather than always-present.

errorNumber.description: Error code, if the action failed.

ipAddress.description: IP address from which the action was performed.

sessionId.description: Session identifier associated with the event, if applicable. Not observed in any events during live testing across all event types (`user_activity`, `access_control`, `int`, `conn_mgmt`, `comment`). The field may be populated only for specific event categories or tenant configurations.

hostName.description: Hostname of the server that recorded the event.

serviceVersion.description: Version of the Anaplan service that generated the event.

eventDate.description: Timestamp when the event occurred (Unix milliseconds, UTC).

createdDate.description: Timestamp when the event was stored in the audit database (Unix milliseconds, UTC).

checksum.description: Checksum for verifying event record integrity. Returned as a short numeric string, not a SHA-256 hash.

searchAuditEvents.description:
Minimum role: Tenant Auditor.

Retrieves audit events for the tenant associated with the authenticated user using a JSON request body to specify the time range. Use `from`/`to` for a specific date range, or `interval` for a rolling window in hours. Use `type` query parameter to filter by event category.

**HIGH VOLUME** — audit events are unbounded. A single busy hour can exceed 1,500 events (~825 KB). With no date filter, the default window is the previous 30 days. With no `limit`, a client that auto-follows `meta.paging` merges every page into one response and overflows its token budget. Always pass an explicit `limit` (start small, ~50–100) and narrow the query with `type` plus a tight time range (`intervalInHours`/`interval` or explicit dates). To sweep the full set, hand-page with `limit`+`offset` or filter server-side — never pull a whole window in one call. CEF output (`Accept: text/plain`) ignores `limit`/`offset` and always returns the entire window.

Set `Accept: text/plain` to receive results in Common Event Format (CEF). Default is `application/json`.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Type of events to return. Same vocabulary as the `type` filter on `GET /events` (each value matches an `eventTypeId` prefix): `all`, `user_activity`, `access_control`, `int`, `conn_mgmt`, `comment`, `byok`, `plan_iq`, `forecaster`. Omitting the parameter is equivalent to `all` (the default). The enum is not enforced server-side.

schema.description: Request body for the POST /events/search endpoint. Specify `from`/`to` for a date range or `interval` for a rolling window. If `to` is omitted, results up to the current time are returned. If `from` is omitted, results from the earliest available event are returned.

from.description: Start of the event date range (Unix timestamp in milliseconds, UTC).

to.description: End of the event date range (Unix timestamp in milliseconds, UTC).

interval.description: Return events from the previous N hours.
